questions.promptText:
An online grocery retailer's demand forecasting team uses a Git repository for training and inference code. A build project currently creates container images when developers merge code. The team now needs a release process that separates build automation from deployment orchestration, runs validation before any endpoint update, and prevents production changes until a reviewer approves the candidate model. The team wants managed AWS services instead of custom deployment logic in the build project.

Which TWO actions meet these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to approve candidate models and start endpoint deployment when drift is detected.
Use AWS CodePipeline to coordinate source, build, validation, and deployment stages, with CodeBuild used for build and test actions.
Schedule an EventBridge rule to run the training job and overwrite the endpoint configuration at fixed intervals.
Use a single CodeBuild buildspec to train the model and update the production endpoint after each successful build.
Configure the release workflow to deploy only model packages that are approved in SageMaker Model Registry.

correctText: Use AWS CodePipeline to coordinate source, build, validation, and deployment stages, with CodeBuild used for build and test actions.
Configure the release workflow to deploy only model packages that are approved in SageMaker Model Registry.
questions.explanationHtml:
CodeBuild and CodePipeline solve different parts of a CI/CD workflow. CodeBuild is a managed build service that can compile code, run tests, and create artifacts. CodePipeline is the orchestration layer that connects source, build, validation, approval, and deployment stages into a controlled release process.

For ML workloads, production deployment should usually be tied to a model governance step rather than simply pushing the latest artifact. SageMaker Model Registry provides a managed place to track model versions and approval status, so a deployment workflow can require an approved candidate before updating an endpoint. This is especially important because a model artifact can be technically deployable but still fail model-specific validation or business review.

The common anti-pattern is to put all release behavior into a build script. That approach is simple at first, but it mixes building, testing, approval, and production deployment into one job and makes controlled promotion difficult. EventBridge and Model Monitor can participate in MLOps workflows, but they do not replace a CI/CD orchestrator and an approval gate for model releases.

For more information, see Continuous integration and continuous delivery in CodePipeline, SageMaker-provided MLOps project templates, Why use MLOps with SageMaker Projects?, and SageMaker AI workflow services.

questions.promptHtml: A wildlife conservation nonprofit's ML team stores millions of camera-trap images in Amazon S3. The team needs labels for an image classification training dataset. The images include confidential habitat locations, so only staff biologists are allowed to view the images. The team wants a managed labeling workflow that can reduce the amount of human labeling as labeling progresses. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
questions.promptText:
A wildlife conservation nonprofit's ML team stores millions of camera-trap images in Amazon S3. The team needs labels for an image classification training dataset. The images include confidential habitat locations, so only staff biologists are allowed to view the images. The team wants a managed labeling workflow that can reduce the amount of human labeling as labeling progresses.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon A2I human review workflow, route every image, and assign a private review team.
Create one or more SageMaker Ground Truth labeling jobs, enable automated data labeling, and assign a private work team.
Create a Rekognition Custom Labels project, train from the unlabeled images, and export predicted labels.
Create Mechanical Turk HITs for the images, require confidentiality instructions, and export the completed labels.

correctText: Create one or more SageMaker Ground Truth labeling jobs, enable automated data labeling, and assign a private work team.
questions.explanationHtml:
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth is built for creating labeled training datasets by coordinating human labeling work and storing the resulting labels for ML workflows. It supports different workforce choices, including a private workforce, which is the right fit when only approved employees should see the source data. Ground Truth can also use automated data labeling for supported task types, where a model learns from completed human labels and sends fewer examples to humans when confidence is high enough. For a dataset with millions of objects, the practical implementation should use multiple labeling jobs, partition the input data, or request a quota increase as needed rather than assuming the entire corpus fits into one job.

Amazon Mechanical Turk can be useful for public crowdsourcing, but it is not appropriate when confidential images must be restricted to internal staff. Amazon A2I is a human review service for ML predictions, commonly used when production predictions need oversight, not as the primary service for generating an initial labeled dataset. Rekognition Custom Labels can build custom image models, but it depends on labeled training images rather than solving the labeling requirement itself. For more details, see SageMaker Ground Truth overview, Create a Ground Truth labeling job, and Ground Truth workforce management.

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.promptHtml: An aerospace telemetry analytics team is standardizing deployments for Amazon SageMaker inference endpoints. A shared platform stack provisions reusable resources, including an Amazon ECR repository and networking resources. Separate model deployment stacks must provision SageMaker model and endpoint resources and use values from the shared stack. All stacks are deployed in the same AWS account and Region. The team wants consistent, repeatable provisioning through infrastructure as code and wants to avoid manual copying of resource identifiers. Which approach will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
questions.promptText:
An aerospace telemetry analytics team is standardizing deployments for Amazon SageMaker inference endpoints. A shared platform stack provisions reusable resources, including an Amazon ECR repository and networking resources. Separate model deployment stacks must provision SageMaker model and endpoint resources and use values from the shared stack. All stacks are deployed in the same AWS account and Region. The team wants consistent, repeatable provisioning through infrastructure as code and wants to avoid manual copying of resource identifiers.

Which approach will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an AWS CodeBuild project, run AWS CLI commands to create resources, and store shared values in the build logs.
Create an Amazon ECS task, provision the SageMaker resources from container code, and pass shared values as environment variables.
Create AWS CloudFormation stacks, copy shared values from the console, and paste those values into model deployment stack parameters.
Create AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK stacks, export shared values from the platform stack, and import those values into the model deployment stacks.

correctText: Create AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK stacks, export shared values from the platform stack, and import those values into the model deployment stacks.
questions.explanationHtml:
AWS CloudFormation and AWS CDK are appropriate when an ML platform team needs repeatable provisioning rather than one-off scripts or console steps. CloudFormation models AWS resources in templates and provisions them as stacks, while CDK stacks are deployment units that synthesize to CloudFormation stacks. See the CloudFormation overview at CloudFormation overview and the CDK stack model at AWS CDK stacks guide.

For communication between stacks, the platform stack can publish identifiers such as repository names, subnet IDs, security group IDs, or endpoint-related values through Outputs. The model deployment stack can then consume those exported values with a cross-stack import, which avoids manually copying resource identifiers into parameters. The relevant CloudFormation mechanisms are described in CloudFormation Outputs section syntax and Fn::ImportValue reference.

The other approaches replace managed stack relationships with manual or imperative processes. CodeBuild and ECS are useful services in MLOps workflows, but they are not the best mechanism for declaring infrastructure dependencies between stacks. For SageMaker deployments, using infrastructure as code also aligns with repeatable deployment practices for resources such as AWS::SageMaker::Model, endpoint configurations, and endpoints.

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.promptHtml: A university medical center's clinical analytics team has standardized an Amazon SageMaker Pipelines workflow that includes data preprocessing, model training, model evaluation, and model registration. The team has an approved build process and wants the same workflow and supporting permissions deployed into separate development, staging, and production AWS accounts with repeatable change control and without manually recreating the workflow in SageMaker Studio. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST custom orchestration code?
questions.promptText:
A university medical center's clinical analytics team has standardized an Amazon SageMaker Pipelines workflow that includes data preprocessing, model training, model evaluation, and model registration. The team has an approved build process and wants the same workflow and supporting permissions deployed into separate development, staging, and production AWS accounts with repeatable change control and without manually recreating the workflow in SageMaker Studio.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST custom orchestration code?

options.text: Create a SageMaker Project template that provisions source repositories and CI/CD resources, and manually attach the existing workflow in each target account.
Create a CodeBuild project that reads the workflow configuration and invokes each SageMaker processing, training, and registration step in sequence.
Define the SageMaker Pipelines workflow and supporting IAM roles in AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK templates, and deploy the templates into each target account.
Create a Step Functions state machine that orchestrates equivalent SageMaker processing, training, evaluation, and registration tasks for each account.

correctText: Define the SageMaker Pipelines workflow and supporting IAM roles in AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK templates, and deploy the templates into each target account.
questions.explanationHtml:
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines is designed to orchestrate ML workflows such as processing, training, evaluation, and model registration. When a team has already standardized on a SageMaker Pipelines workflow, the lowest-overhead deployment approach is to keep that managed workflow as the unit of automation rather than recreating the same sequence in another service.

Infrastructure as code tools such as AWS CloudFormation and AWS CDK support repeatable, reviewed deployments across accounts and environments. This matches the need for change control in development, staging, and production because the deployment process can promote the same declared infrastructure pattern instead of relying on manual SageMaker Studio actions.

SageMaker Projects are useful when a team wants a broader MLOps scaffold with repositories and CI/CD templates, but they are not the most direct fit when the primary need is repeatable deployment of an already standardized workflow. CodeBuild and Step Functions can participate in ML automation, but using them to reconstruct each ML step increases custom orchestration and can cause the deployed workflow to drift from the managed SageMaker Pipelines design. For more information, see Overview of Amazon SageMaker Pipelines, AWS::SageMaker::Pipeline, and AWS Step Functions integration with SageMaker.

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.promptHtml: A maritime logistics provider's ML platform team maintains inference container code and Amazon SageMaker pipeline definitions in a Git repository. An AWS CodePipeline pipeline currently builds the container image and deploys SageMaker endpoint changes. The team needs automated unit and integration tests to run on every code change and prevent deployment when tests fail. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
questions.promptText: A maritime logistics provider's ML platform team maintains inference container code and Amazon SageMaker pipeline definitions in a Git repository. An AWS CodePipeline pipeline currently builds the container image and deploys SageMaker endpoint changes. The team needs automated unit and integration tests to run on every code change and prevent deployment when tests fail. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Add a SageMaker deployment guardrail before testing, shift canary traffic, and publish endpoint alarm events to CloudWatch.
Add an EventBridge rule on repository changes, invoke a Lambda test runner, and store raw test logs in Amazon S3.
Add a SageMaker Model Monitor schedule before deployment, compare captured endpoint data, and publish violations to CloudWatch.
Add a CodeBuild test action before deployment, run the suites in CodeBuild, and fail the action on test failures.

correctText: Add a CodeBuild test action before deployment, run the suites in CodeBuild, and fail the action on test failures.
questions.explanationHtml:
AWS CodePipeline is the orchestration layer for CI/CD workflows, where changes move through stages such as source, build, test, and deploy. In this scenario, the pipeline already exists, so the lowest-overhead approach is to add a CodeBuild action in a test stage before the deployment stage. CodeBuild can run automated unit and integration tests as part of the pipeline, and a failed action prevents later deployment actions from running.

This pattern fits MLOps workflows in which SageMaker model code, container definitions, and pipeline definitions are versioned in a repository and promoted through an automated delivery process. Deployment guardrails and Model Monitor are useful after or during model deployment, but they do not provide a source-code test gate. EventBridge and Lambda could be assembled into a custom solution, but that would add operational overhead compared with using the existing CodePipeline and CodeBuild workflow.

For more information, see What is a pipeline in CodePipeline?, CodeBuild action reference for CodePipeline, and SageMaker Projects overview.

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
questions.promptHtml: A regional sports media network's personalization team hosts a video recommendation model on an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint. The team has a candidate model version and wants to evaluate whether it improves click-through rate and response latency for a limited share of live viewers. Ground truth engagement labels arrive later in the day. The team wants to compare the current and candidate models in production before increasing traffic to the candidate model. The solution must keep a single SageMaker endpoint and must not require changes to application routing logic. Which TWO actions will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
A regional sports media network's personalization team hosts a video recommendation model on an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint. The team has a candidate model version and wants to evaluate whether it improves click-through rate and response latency for a limited share of live viewers. Ground truth engagement labels arrive later in the day. The team wants to compare the current and candidate models in production before increasing traffic to the candidate model. The solution must keep a single SageMaker endpoint and must not require changes to application routing logic.

Which TWO actions will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a batch transform job for both models, and compare offline predictions against the next day's engagement labels.
Compare CloudWatch metrics and captured inference records by production variant before shifting more traffic to the candidate model.
Deploy the candidate model to a separate endpoint, and modify the application to randomly choose an endpoint for each request.
Send all production requests to the candidate model first, and roll back manually if CloudWatch alarms indicate degraded latency.
Configure the endpoint with the current and candidate models as production variants, and assign a small traffic weight to the candidate variant.

correctText: Compare CloudWatch metrics and captured inference records by production variant before shifting more traffic to the candidate model.
Configure the endpoint with the current and candidate models as production variants, and assign a small traffic weight to the candidate variant.
questions.explanationHtml:
A/B testing in Amazon SageMaker uses multiple production variants behind a real-time endpoint. Each variant can host a different model or instance configuration, and SageMaker can route a specified percentage of requests to each variant. This lets an ML operations team evaluate a candidate model with live traffic while keeping most users on the current model.

For monitoring, the team should use Amazon CloudWatch endpoint metrics and captured inference data. CloudWatch helps compare operational behavior such as traffic volume, latency, and errors across variants, while SageMaker Data Capture and Model Monitor can preserve inputs and outputs in Amazon S3 for later analysis when ground truth labels arrive. See Test models in production, Monitor Amazon SageMaker with Amazon CloudWatch, and Capture data from real-time endpoints.

Offline batch transform can be valuable for validation, but it is not a substitute for production A/B testing because it does not measure the live serving path or real viewer behavior. Creating a second endpoint and pushing randomization into the application conflicts with the stated requirement to keep routing managed by SageMaker on one endpoint. Sending all traffic to the new model first is riskier than necessary and does not satisfy the requirement to limit exposure while performance is evaluated.

questions.promptHtml: A renewable energy trading desk trains an Amazon SageMaker binary classification model to predict whether wholesale electricity prices will spike the next day. The team needs a repeatable way to establish a model performance baseline before approving each new model version. Reviewers require metrics from data that was not used during training, and the same process must support comparisons against future candidate models. Which approach will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
A renewable energy trading desk trains an Amazon SageMaker binary classification model to predict whether wholesale electricity prices will spike the next day. The team needs a repeatable way to establish a model performance baseline before approving each new model version. Reviewers require metrics from data that was not used during training, and the same process must support comparisons against future candidate models.

Which approach will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy each candidate model to all production traffic, collect the first day of predictions, and use those results as the approval baseline.
Add a SageMaker Pipelines evaluation step that scores a held-out test set, calculates classification metrics, and stores the metrics with the model package.
Configure the SageMaker training job to publish training accuracy to Amazon CloudWatch, and approve models when the training metric improves.
Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query inference latency logs, and use p95 latency as the model quality baseline for approvals.

correctText: Add a SageMaker Pipelines evaluation step that scores a held-out test set, calculates classification metrics, and stores the metrics with the model package.
questions.explanationHtml:
A practical model performance baseline should measure how well a trained model performs on data that was not used to fit the model. For a binary classifier, relevant baseline metrics commonly include precision, recall, F1 score, and accuracy, depending on the business tradeoff. In SageMaker, a repeatable pattern is to place evaluation into an automated workflow, such as a SageMaker Pipelines step, and store the resulting metrics with the model artifact or model package so future versions can be compared consistently.

Training metrics emitted during the training job can help diagnose convergence or overfitting, but they are not a substitute for an evaluation baseline on unseen data. Production variants and A/B testing are valuable for online validation, but they usually come after a candidate has passed offline evaluation. Model Monitor can later use model quality baselines and ground-truth labels to detect drift in production, but the baseline still depends on meaningful predictions and labels. For more information, see Model validation in Amazon SageMaker, Monitor and analyze training jobs using Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and Create a model quality baseline.

questions.promptHtml: An international hotel group's loyalty analytics team is preparing an ML training dataset from guest profiles, reservation history, and free-text service notes that are stored in Amazon S3. The raw data contains names, email addresses, phone numbers, loyalty identifiers, and special request notes. Compliance requires the team to find sensitive data in the S3 data lake, prevent raw PII from being included in the training dataset, and store the curated training output only in the approved AWS Region. Which combination of steps should the team take? (Select TWO.)
questions.promptText:
An international hotel group's loyalty analytics team is preparing an ML training dataset from guest profiles, reservation history, and free-text service notes that are stored in Amazon S3. The raw data contains names, email addresses, phone numbers, loyalty identifiers, and special request notes. Compliance requires the team to find sensitive data in the S3 data lake, prevent raw PII from being included in the training dataset, and store the curated training output only in the approved AWS Region.

Which combination of steps should the team take? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Run Amazon Macie discovery jobs on the S3 buckets to identify objects that contain sensitive data.
Use Amazon Athena views to hide sensitive columns while allowing the training job to read the original S3 objects.
Register trained model versions in Amazon SageMaker Model Registry after the training workflow completes.
Replicate the raw S3 objects to buckets in multiple Regions before running the data preparation workflow.
Apply AWS Glue DataBrew PII transformations to mask or delete sensitive fields and write the output to S3 in the approved Region.

correctText: Run Amazon Macie discovery jobs on the S3 buckets to identify objects that contain sensitive data.
Apply AWS Glue DataBrew PII transformations to mask or delete sensitive fields and write the output to S3 in the approved Region.
questions.explanationHtml:
For ML data preparation under compliance constraints, separate the problem into two controls: discover where sensitive data exists and produce a sanitized training dataset. Amazon Macie is appropriate for discovering sensitive data in Amazon S3, including common PII patterns, so the team can identify risky buckets and objects before feature engineering begins. See Amazon Macie managed data identifiers.

After discovery, the team still needs to transform the data. AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual data preparation tool that can profile datasets and apply PII-oriented transformations such as masking, hashing, encryption, nulling, or deletion. The curated result should be written to S3 only in the approved AWS Region so downstream training jobs use the sanitized data rather than the raw source records. The related AWS Glue sensitive data capabilities are described in Detect and process sensitive data in AWS Glue.

A common anti-pattern is to rely only on query-time filtering while leaving training pipelines pointed at raw data. That might reduce what some users see in one query path, but it does not create a clean ML training artifact and can lead to accidental leakage through another consumer. Similarly, copying raw PII into additional Regions before transformation increases compliance risk and directly works against a data residency requirement.

questions.promptHtml: A biomedical device manufacturer's quality analytics team prepares monthly ML training extracts from a relational quality system. Each extract is a small tabular file that quality engineers review in spreadsheet tools before the file is loaded into Amazon S3 for downstream experiments. The team values simple interchange with non-engineering users and does not need to optimize large analytical scans. Which data format should the team use for these extracts?
questions.promptText:
A biomedical device manufacturer's quality analytics team prepares monthly ML training extracts from a relational quality system. Each extract is a small tabular file that quality engineers review in spreadsheet tools before the file is loaded into Amazon S3 for downstream experiments. The team values simple interchange with non-engineering users and does not need to optimize large analytical scans.

Which data format should the team use for these extracts?

options.text: Write the monthly extracts as CSV files with consistent column names and delimiters.
Write the monthly extracts as ORC files with columnar storage for analytics.
Write the monthly extracts as JSON files with one nested object per record.
Write the monthly extracts as Parquet files with columnar encoding and compression.

correctText: Write the monthly extracts as CSV files with consistent column names and delimiters.
questions.explanationHtml:
For data preparation, the best format depends on the access pattern, not on a single universally best storage choice. CSV is a practical choice for small, fixed-schema tabular data that people need to inspect, exchange, or edit with common tools. It is human readable and widely supported, which reduces friction when non-engineering users participate in data review.

Columnar formats such as Parquet and ORC are often better for large analytical datasets because engines can read selected columns efficiently and reduce scanned data. That tradeoff matters for workloads such as Amazon Athena or Redshift Spectrum queries over large S3 datasets, but it is not the priority in this scenario. AWS documents these columnar-format benefits in Amazon Athena guidance on when to use columnar formats such as Parquet and ORC, and AWS Glue lists supported ETL formats, including CSV, JSON, Parquet, and ORC, in AWS Glue documentation for ETL input and output data formats.

questions.promptHtml: A public transit authority's analytics team trains a neural network in Amazon SageMaker to predict whether a bus route will miss its on-time target. The model reaches high accuracy on the training dataset, but its accuracy is much lower on a held-out validation dataset. The team wants to improve performance on new route data without collecting additional data or adding new features. Which action should the ML engineer take?
questions.promptText:
A public transit authority's analytics team trains a neural network in Amazon SageMaker to predict whether a bus route will miss its on-time target. The model reaches high accuracy on the training dataset, but its accuracy is much lower on a held-out validation dataset. The team wants to improve performance on new route data without collecting additional data or adding new features.

Which action should the ML engineer take?

options.text: Reduce dropout in the network and decrease L2 weight decay during retraining.
Optimize only for training accuracy and select the run with the highest score.
Add more hidden layers to the network and increase the number of epochs.
Increase dropout in the network and tune L2 weight decay during retraining.

correctText: Increase dropout in the network and tune L2 weight decay during retraining.
questions.explanationHtml:
When a model performs much better on training data than on held-out validation data, the practical concern is overfitting. Regularization techniques deliberately constrain the model so it is less likely to learn noise or accidental patterns in the training set.

Dropout randomly disables a fraction of neural network units during training, which discourages codependent behavior among neurons. L2 regularization, often implemented as weight decay, penalizes large weights and tends to produce smoother models that generalize better.

Adding layers or training for more epochs increases model capacity or training exposure, which can worsen overfitting if no additional controls are applied. Optimizing only for training accuracy is also risky because the goal is not memorization, it is performance on unseen data.

The AWS exam guide explicitly includes the AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate Domain 2 outline skill area for regularization techniques. AWS documentation also describes regularization as a way to address overfitting in Model Fit: Underfitting vs. Overfitting, and documents SageMaker examples such as dropout in Object2Vec Hyperparameters and wd as weight decay in Linear Learner Hyperparameters.

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
questions.promptHtml: An automotive warranty analytics team hosts a fraud risk model on an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint. The team has baseline statistics from the training dataset, but confirmed fraud labels can take several weeks to arrive. The team wants daily alerts when production request features show distribution shifts, missing or unexpected features, or unusual values before labels are available. The solution must require the least custom monitoring code. Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
An automotive warranty analytics team hosts a fraud risk model on an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint. The team has baseline statistics from the training dataset, but confirmed fraud labels can take several weeks to arrive. The team wants daily alerts when production request features show distribution shifts, missing or unexpected features, or unusual values before labels are available. The solution must require the least custom monitoring code.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable Data Capture, configure model quality checks only, and publish accuracy metrics to CloudWatch alarms each day.
Enable Data Capture, create a baseline from the training dataset, and schedule SageMaker Model Monitor data quality checks with CloudWatch alarms.
Analyze CloudTrail management events for the SageMaker endpoint and trigger EventBridge notifications for unusual write activity.
Create CloudWatch dashboards for endpoint invocations, latency, CPU, and memory, and alarm on abnormal endpoint utilization.

correctText: Enable Data Capture, create a baseline from the training dataset, and schedule SageMaker Model Monitor data quality checks with CloudWatch alarms.
questions.explanationHtml:
SageMaker Model Monitor is designed to monitor deployed models by running scheduled monitoring jobs against captured inference data. For this scenario, the key constraint is that labels are not available for weeks, so the practical first signal is whether live input data still resembles the training baseline. Data quality monitoring compares production features with baseline statistics and constraints, then emits metrics that can be used with CloudWatch alarms.

Data Capture records inference inputs and outputs from a SageMaker endpoint to Amazon S3, which gives monitoring jobs data to analyze without adding custom logging code to the application. This captured data can also support debugging and later retraining workflows. See Capture data from real-time endpoints and Monitor data quality.

Model quality monitoring is valuable when ground truth labels are available because it can track performance metrics such as accuracy-related measures for classification or regression metrics for regression workloads. However, it is not the best answer when the requirement is to detect problems before delayed labels arrive. CloudWatch endpoint metrics and CloudTrail events remain important for operations and auditing, but they do not inspect the statistical quality of model input features. For a broader view of monitoring types, see Monitor models for data and model quality, bias, and feature attribution drift.

questions.promptHtml: A municipal tax agency's compliance analytics team is building a binary classification model in Amazon SageMaker AI to flag filings for possible audit. The dataset is tabular, labeled, normalized, and shuffled. The agency must catch at least a specified percentage of truly noncompliant filings, but within that constraint wants to reduce the number of compliant filings sent to audit. The team wants to use a SageMaker AI built-in algorithm with minimal custom code. Which approach should the team use?
questions.promptText:
A municipal tax agency's compliance analytics team is building a binary classification model in Amazon SageMaker AI to flag filings for possible audit. The dataset is tabular, labeled, normalized, and shuffled. The agency must catch at least a specified percentage of truly noncompliant filings, but within that constraint wants to reduce the number of compliant filings sent to audit. The team wants to use a SageMaker AI built-in algorithm with minimal custom code.

Which approach should the team use?

options.text: Train a SageMaker AI K-Means model, set the number of clusters to two, and label the higher-risk cluster as the audit class.
Train a SageMaker AI Linear Learner binary classifier, set the model selection criteria to precision at target recall, and configure the required target recall.
Train a SageMaker AI XGBoost model, set the evaluation metric to RMSE, and select the training job with the lowest validation error.
Train a SageMaker AI Linear Learner binary classifier, set the model selection criteria to recall at target precision, and configure the audit precision target.

correctText: Train a SageMaker AI Linear Learner binary classifier, set the model selection criteria to precision at target recall, and configure the required target recall.
questions.explanationHtml:
Recall measures how many actual positive cases the model catches, so it is the right constraint when missing a positive case is the more serious failure. In this scenario, the positive class is a truly noncompliant filing, and the agency must catch at least a specified percentage of those cases. Once that recall requirement is met, improving precision reduces the number of compliant filings incorrectly sent to audit.

For a labeled tabular binary classification problem, SageMaker AI built-in algorithms can reduce implementation effort because the team can use managed training rather than maintaining its own algorithm container. Linear Learner is suitable when the team wants a built-in supervised algorithm for regression or classification and the data has already been prepared appropriately. Its target recall and target precision settings are designed for this kind of practical model-selection tradeoff, where the business requirement is not simply highest overall accuracy.

The opposite Linear Learner setting would optimize recall while holding precision fixed, which is not the same operational requirement. XGBoost is also a common SageMaker AI algorithm for tabular data, but choosing RMSE does not express the recall constraint. K-Means is plausible only if the team lacked labels and wanted exploratory clustering, but this scenario has labels and needs supervised binary classification behavior.

For more about SageMaker AI algorithm choices and training options, see Use Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms or pre-trained models and Train a model with Amazon SageMaker.

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.promptHtml: A national grocery chain's demand forecasting team manages Amazon SageMaker Pipelines definitions and inference container code in a GitHub repository. The team has standardized on GitHub Flow: short-lived feature branches, pull requests, and a main branch that is always deployable. The team wants merges into main to automatically build and test the container image, run the SageMaker model build pipeline, and start the deployment workflow. The team wants to use managed AWS CI/CD services with the least custom orchestration. Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
A national grocery chain's demand forecasting team manages Amazon SageMaker Pipelines definitions and inference container code in a GitHub repository. The team has standardized on GitHub Flow: short-lived feature branches, pull requests, and a main branch that is always deployable. The team wants merges into main to automatically build and test the container image, run the SageMaker model build pipeline, and start the deployment workflow. The team wants to use managed AWS CI/CD services with the least custom orchestration.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a SageMaker Project with CodePipeline connected to GitHub, trigger the pipeline on pushes to develop, and merge develop into main after the deployment workflow.
Create a SageMaker Project with CodePipeline connected to GitHub, trigger the pipeline on pushes to main, and run CodeBuild steps for the SageMaker build and deployment workflow.
Create a Lambda function to poll GitHub pull requests continuously, and invoke CodeDeploy directly when a pull request is opened against main.
Create an EventBridge scheduled rule to start the SageMaker Pipeline hourly, and configure the pipeline to pull the latest main branch commit during execution.

correctText: Create a SageMaker Project with CodePipeline connected to GitHub, trigger the pipeline on pushes to main, and run CodeBuild steps for the SageMaker build and deployment workflow.
questions.explanationHtml:
GitHub Flow treats main as the deployable branch, so the automation should be tied to changes that land on main, not to a separate long-lived integration branch. In an AWS ML workflow, SageMaker Projects can provide the MLOps scaffolding around source control, model build pipelines, model registry usage, and deployment automation.

CodePipeline is the managed orchestration layer for a sequence such as source, build, test, provision, and deploy. A source connection to GitHub can start a pipeline from repository events, and branch filters let the team align the trigger with the selected branching strategy. See GitHub connections and pipeline triggers.

Using a develop branch would be more consistent with Gitflow, not the stated GitHub Flow process. Using a schedule or a custom polling Lambda function separates deployment from the actual Git event, adds custom orchestration, and can make traceability from commit to pipeline run less direct. For more context on branch patterns, see Git branching strategies and SageMaker Projects.

questions.promptHtml: A satellite imagery startup's ML team has a custom PyTorch training script that trains a convolutional neural network. The team wants to run the training job on Amazon SageMaker AI managed training infrastructure. The team wants to use a SageMaker AI supported framework container and avoid maintaining a custom Docker image. The training data is stored in Amazon S3, and the trained model artifacts must be available in Amazon S3 after training. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
questions.promptText:
A satellite imagery startup's ML team has a custom PyTorch training script that trains a convolutional neural network. The team wants to run the training job on Amazon SageMaker AI managed training infrastructure. The team wants to use a SageMaker AI supported framework container and avoid maintaining a custom Docker image. The training data is stored in Amazon S3, and the trained model artifacts must be available in Amazon S3 after training.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Create a SageMaker AI PyTorch estimator that specifies the training script as the entry point.
Configure the training job to read input channels from Amazon S3 and write model output to Amazon S3.
Build a custom Docker image that includes PyTorch, the training script, and all runtime dependencies.
Select the SageMaker AI Linear Learner built-in algorithm and provide the PyTorch script as a training parameter.
Run the PyTorch script on an Amazon EC2 instance and copy the completed model artifacts into Amazon S3.

correctText: Create a SageMaker AI PyTorch estimator that specifies the training script as the entry point.
Configure the training job to read input channels from Amazon S3 and write model output to Amazon S3.
questions.explanationHtml:
SageMaker AI script mode is designed for cases where you have custom training code, such as a .py script, but do not want to build an entire container yourself. You use a SageMaker supported framework estimator, such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, and provide an entry_point script. SageMaker supplies the prebuilt framework container and manages the training job infrastructure.

In a managed SageMaker training workflow, training data is typically stored in Amazon S3, and the training job writes model artifacts back to S3 when training completes. This separates the code, compute, input data, and output artifacts cleanly, which is why SageMaker can spin up training resources for the job and tear them down afterward.

Building a custom Docker image is useful when the built-in framework containers do not meet your needs, but it is unnecessary overhead in this scenario. Built-in algorithms are also not the right fit because they are prepackaged algorithm implementations, not a way to run arbitrary PyTorch code. Running training manually on Amazon EC2 is a valid general compute pattern, but it gives up the managed training lifecycle that SageMaker provides.

For more information, see Use machine learning algorithms in Amazon SageMaker AI, Use PyTorch with Amazon SageMaker AI, and Use Docker containers with SageMaker AI.

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
questions.promptHtml: An online education platform's learner success team hosts an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint that predicts whether a learner will complete a paid certification course. The platform is about to onboard large corporate cohorts from new countries. The governance team needs scheduled monitoring that compares live inference traffic with a baseline from training data and sends alerts when distribution changes could introduce unfair outcomes for a protected learner attribute. The team wants to avoid building custom drift detection code. Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
An online education platform's learner success team hosts an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint that predicts whether a learner will complete a paid certification course. The platform is about to onboard large corporate cohorts from new countries. The governance team needs scheduled monitoring that compares live inference traffic with a baseline from training data and sends alerts when distribution changes could introduce unfair outcomes for a protected learner attribute. The team wants to avoid building custom drift detection code.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure SageMaker Clarify bias drift monitoring with a training baseline and CloudWatch alerts.
Configure SageMaker Model Monitor data quality monitoring with only feature statistics alerts.
Configure CloudTrail Insights to detect unusual endpoint invocation patterns and send EventBridge alerts.
Configure SageMaker Experiments to compare retraining runs and publish trial metrics to dashboards.

correctText: Configure SageMaker Clarify bias drift monitoring with a training baseline and CloudWatch alerts.
questions.explanationHtml:
SageMaker Clarify is the best fit when the monitoring concern is whether changes in live data can affect fairness or bias-related behavior after a model is deployed. In this scenario, the organization is not merely asking whether feature distributions changed, it is asking whether those changes could create unfair outcomes for a protected attribute, so bias drift monitoring is the managed capability that aligns with the requirement.

SageMaker Model Monitor provides the recurring monitoring framework: it can use captured inference data, compare that data with baselines, emit metrics to CloudWatch, and support alerting workflows. Clarify extends this monitoring approach for responsible AI use cases, including bias drift and feature attribution drift, rather than only generic data quality checks. See Overview of Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor and Monitor bias drift for models in production.

Data quality monitoring is still useful when the goal is to detect changes in the statistical nature of production data compared with baseline data, as described in Monitor data quality. However, feature statistics alone do not answer the governance question about bias for a protected attribute. CloudTrail Insights and SageMaker Experiments are also valuable operational tools, but they address API activity anomalies and experiment tracking, not managed production bias drift detection.

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.promptHtml: A marine insurance underwriting analytics team retrains a risk model weekly. The workflow runs an Amazon SageMaker Processing job for feature preparation, a SageMaker training job, an evaluation step, model registration, and an endpoint update after approval. The team wants the workflow definition to be version controlled, visible from SageMaker Studio, and tied to model lineage. The team does not need to orchestrate unrelated ETL or analytics workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
questions.promptText:
A marine insurance underwriting analytics team retrains a risk model weekly. The workflow runs an Amazon SageMaker Processing job for feature preparation, a SageMaker training job, an evaluation step, model registration, and an endpoint update after approval. The team wants the workflow definition to be version controlled, visible from SageMaker Studio, and tied to model lineage. The team does not need to orchestrate unrelated ETL or analytics workloads.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Implement the workflow with Amazon MWAA and upload Python DAG files to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Implement the workflow with AWS Step Functions and call SageMaker job APIs from state machine tasks.
Implement the workflow with AWS CodePipeline and run SageMaker job scripts from AWS CodeBuild stages.
Implement the workflow with Amazon SageMaker Pipelines and define the model lifecycle tasks as pipeline steps.

correctText: Implement the workflow with Amazon SageMaker Pipelines and define the model lifecycle tasks as pipeline steps.
questions.explanationHtml:
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines is the best fit when the workflow is primarily an ML lifecycle workflow inside SageMaker. It is purpose-built for steps such as preprocessing, training, evaluation, model registration, and deployment-related automation, and it is integrated with SageMaker Studio and SageMaker lineage concepts. See the AWS documentation for Amazon SageMaker Pipelines and defining a SageMaker pipeline.

Amazon MWAA is a managed Apache Airflow service, and it is a strong choice when a team already standardizes on Airflow or needs to coordinate many non-ML workflows across ETL, analytics, storage, and databases. In this scenario, the requirements point to a SageMaker-native model build and deployment workflow rather than a broad enterprise scheduler. The MWAA model of storing and running DAGs from Amazon S3 is described in working with DAGs in Amazon MWAA.

AWS Step Functions can orchestrate SageMaker jobs and endpoint operations, so it is a plausible alternative for service-level workflow coordination. However, for a model lifecycle workflow that needs SageMaker Studio visibility and lineage with minimal custom integration, SageMaker Pipelines is the more direct choice. Step Functions SageMaker integrations are documented in SageMaker AI service integrations for Step Functions.

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.promptHtml: A pharmaceutical research lab hosts a model on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint for an internal compound screening application. Traffic is low most of the day but has short bursts when scientists submit screening jobs, and the application must continue to receive low-latency responses. The lab also retrains the model nightly, and those retraining jobs can tolerate interruption if progress is preserved. The team wants to improve scalability and reduce cost with minimal operational overhead. Which TWO actions should the team take?
questions.promptText:
A pharmaceutical research lab hosts a model on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint for an internal compound screening application. Traffic is low most of the day but has short bursts when scientists submit screening jobs, and the application must continue to receive low-latency responses. The lab also retrains the model nightly, and those retraining jobs can tolerate interruption if progress is preserved. The team wants to improve scalability and reduce cost with minimal operational overhead.

Which TWO actions should the team take?

options.text: Invoke the endpoint through AWS Lambda and use Lambda reserved concurrency as the only scaling control.
Replace the real-time endpoint with SageMaker Batch Transform for all screening requests.
Configure automatic scaling for the SageMaker AI endpoint with minimum and maximum variant capacity.
Increase the endpoint to the expected peak instance count and disable scaling policies.
Enable SageMaker Managed Spot Training for retraining jobs and configure checkpointing for recovery.

correctText: Configure automatic scaling for the SageMaker AI endpoint with minimum and maximum variant capacity.
Enable SageMaker Managed Spot Training for retraining jobs and configure checkpointing for recovery.
questions.explanationHtml:
For a real-time inference workload that must preserve low latency but has bursty traffic, the scalable managed approach is to keep the SageMaker AI endpoint and configure endpoint automatic scaling. SageMaker endpoint scaling adjusts the number of instances for a production variant within configured bounds, which lets the endpoint keep baseline capacity while scaling out for bursts and scaling back when demand falls. See SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling policy overview.

For the nightly retraining workload, SageMaker Managed Spot Training is a good cost optimization when interruption is acceptable. The important operational companion is checkpointing, because Spot capacity can be interrupted and the training job should be able to resume from saved state instead of wasting completed work. See SageMaker Managed Spot Training.

The other approaches confuse adjacent scaling mechanisms with the actual bottleneck. Batch Transform is appropriate when predictions can be produced offline for an entire dataset, not when an application needs low-latency responses. Keeping peak endpoint capacity running all day is a common cost anti-pattern for bursty workloads, and Lambda reserved concurrency does not scale the SageMaker endpoint fleet itself.

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
questions.promptHtml: A regional electric utility's grid reliability team hosts an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint that predicts whether transformers will fail within 30 days. The team captures inference inputs and predictions. Actual maintenance outcomes are loaded into Amazon S3 once each week. The team wants automated alerts when the deployed model's predictive performance degrades compared with an approved baseline, with the least custom monitoring code. Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
A regional electric utility's grid reliability team hosts an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint that predicts whether transformers will fail within 30 days. The team captures inference inputs and predictions. Actual maintenance outcomes are loaded into Amazon S3 once each week. The team wants automated alerts when the deployed model's predictive performance degrades compared with an approved baseline, with the least custom monitoring code.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure SageMaker Model Monitor with a model quality baseline, provide ground truth labels, and create CloudWatch alarms for monitoring violations.
Configure CloudTrail Insights for SageMaker write events, route EventBridge events, and create SNS notifications for unusual activity.
Configure SageMaker Model Monitor with a data quality baseline, compare request feature statistics, and create CloudWatch alarms for monitoring violations.
Configure SageMaker Clarify bias drift monitoring, compare bias metrics against a baseline, and create CloudWatch alarms for monitoring violations.

correctText: Configure SageMaker Model Monitor with a model quality baseline, provide ground truth labels, and create CloudWatch alarms for monitoring violations.
questions.explanationHtml:
Drift can mean different things in an ML system. If production feature distributions change, that is typically handled as data quality drift. If the model's actual predictive performance changes after comparing predictions to real outcomes, that is model quality drift.

In this scenario, the team receives actual maintenance outcomes weekly, so the best fit is Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor model quality monitoring. The monitoring process can compare captured predictions with ground truth labels, evaluate performance against a baseline, and emit metrics that can be used with Amazon CloudWatch alarms. See Overview of Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor and Monitor model quality.

Data quality monitoring is still useful, but it answers a different question: whether inference-time input features have statistically shifted from the baseline. SageMaker Clarify bias drift monitoring is for bias-related changes, and CloudTrail Insights is for unusual AWS account activity, not ML prediction quality.

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.promptHtml: A sports analytics provider's prediction services team hosts a player injury risk model on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. The team releases a new model version every two weeks. The team wants to expose the new version to only a small portion of live requests initially, monitor operational metrics during the rollout, and automatically return traffic to the current version if alarms are triggered. The team wants the lowest operational effort for rollback. Which deployment approach should the team use?
questions.promptText:
A sports analytics provider's prediction services team hosts a player injury risk model on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. The team releases a new model version every two weeks. The team wants to expose the new version to only a small portion of live requests initially, monitor operational metrics during the rollout, and automatically return traffic to the current version if alarms are triggered. The team wants the lowest operational effort for rollback.

Which deployment approach should the team use?

options.text: Configure a SageMaker AI shadow test to mirror production requests to the new model and promote the shadow variant when metrics look acceptable.
Configure SageMaker AI deployment guardrails to shift all traffic to the new fleet immediately and review endpoint metrics after the baking period.
Configure production variant weights to route a small fixed share to the new model and manually reset weights if errors increase.
Configure SageMaker AI deployment guardrails to shift an initial small traffic portion to the new fleet and attach CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback.

correctText: Configure SageMaker AI deployment guardrails to shift an initial small traffic portion to the new fleet and attach CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback.
questions.explanationHtml:
SageMaker AI deployment guardrails are designed for safer production model updates on real-time and asynchronous inference endpoints. They let teams use blue/green style deployments with traffic shifting patterns such as all-at-once, canary, and linear, then monitor the new fleet during a baking period before completing the update.

For this scenario, the key requirement is to send only a small amount of live traffic to the new model at first and to roll back automatically if monitored conditions fail. A canary rollout fits that pattern because it starts with limited exposure, observes the new deployment, and can return traffic to the blue fleet when CloudWatch alarms are triggered. See SageMaker AI overview of deployment guardrails for production model updates and SageMaker AI canary traffic shifting.

An all-at-once deployment is simpler, but it moves the entire workload immediately, which is not appropriate when the team wants to minimize initial blast radius. A linear deployment can also reduce risk by shifting traffic gradually, but the stated need for a small initial live exposure with managed rollback is most directly aligned with canary traffic shifting. Shadow testing is different: it helps compare a shadow variant against production traffic without serving the shadow model's predictions to users, and promotion is a decision the team makes after reviewing results.

Automatic rollback depends on monitoring signals, typically through CloudWatch alarms configured for the deployment. The managed rollback behavior is preferable to manually resetting production variant weights because it reduces response time and operational burden when a deployment begins to fail. For rollback configuration details, see SageMaker AI auto-rollback configuration and monitoring with CloudWatch alarms.
